about: Instance types commonly used to run a mover, as their providers publish them. network_gbps and disk_mb_s give the baseline a long move runs at and the burst a short one may reach for burst_minutes; price_hour is the on-demand Linux price in USD per hour by region. Burstable-CPU types (AWS t, Azure B) are left out: a long move runs at their CPU baseline, a fraction of a core. Refreshed from the provider's own API where credentials are present (migkit.machine.refresh).

notes.aws: network burst lasts typically from 5 to 60 minutes by instance size, on a best-effort basis: 5 is taken; EBS-optimized burst lasts 30 minutes at least once every 24 hours
notes.gcp: egress is a ceiling with no credit to burst on, so baseline and burst are the same; disk is a persistent disk's write bandwidth with the network busy, by vCPU count, capped at a balanced disk's 1,200 MiB/s an instance; prices are us-central1 (the pages' default region)
notes.azure: network is the published maximum with no credit to burst on; disk is uncached Premium SSD throughput, with credit bursting up to 30 minutes
